==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|conquere|conquire||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|conqueren}}, from {{der|en|fro|conquerre}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|conquaero|conquaerere|to knock, strike; to search for, procure}}, from {{der|en|la|con-}} + {{m|la|quaero|quaerere|to seek, acquire}}. Displaced native {{ncog|ang|oferwinnan}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɒŋkə/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈkɑŋkɚ/|a=GA}}
* {{hyph|en|con|quer}}
* {{rhymes|en|ɒŋkə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-conquer.ogg|a=US}}
* {{homophone|en|conker}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To [[defeat]] in [[combat]]; to [[subjugate]].
#: {{syn|en|overrun}}
#* {{RQ:Dunsany Pegana||88|I lay in the desert beyond all cities and sounds, and above me flowed the River of Silence through the sky; and on the desert’s edge night fought against the Sun, and suddenly '''conquered'''.}}
# To become a [[leader]], [[decisive]] factor or [[champion]] in an area.
#: {{ux|en|With her successes, she has truly '''conquered''' the committee, all of whose members now defer to her on most issues.}}
#: {{ux|en|It was his campaign manager's strategy that truly '''conquered''' the election for him.}}
#: {{ux|en|By the end of the season, he had '''conquered''' the sport of baseball.}}
# To [[acquire]] by force of arms, [[win]] in [[war]]; to become ruler of; to subjugate.
#: {{ux|en|In 1453, the Ottoman Empire '''conquered''' Constantinople.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare Venus and Adonis|year=1594|verse=17|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PyHPAAAAMAAJ&pg=PP13|lines=97–100|passage=I haue beene wooed, as I intreat thee now, / Euen by the ſterne, and direfull God of warre, / VVhoſe [[sinewy|ſinowie]] necke in battel [[ne'er|nere]] did bow, / VVho '''conquers''' where he comes in euery [[jar|iarre]]; {{...}}}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1714|author=w:Alexander Pope|title=Imitation of Horace, Book II. Sat. 6
|passage=We '''conquer'd''' France, but felt our captive's charms.}}
#* {{RQ:Doyle Lost World|passage="Look at Clive - just a clerk, and he '''conquered''' India!"}}
#* {{quote-book|en
|year=1992
|author=w:Richard Nixon
|chapter=The Pacific Triangle
|title=Seize the Moment
|url=https://archive.org/details/seizemomentameri00nixo/
|publisher=w:Simon & Schuster
|ISBN=0-671-74343-0
|LCCN=91-37743
|OCLC=440652941
|page=170
|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/seizemomentameri00nixo/page/170/
|text=Taiwan's interests and Hong Kong's political and economic future are best served by close ties between their friends in the West and Beijing. For example, the fact that the PRC must choose between using force to '''conquer''' Taiwan and forfeiting its relationship with the United States is the best guarantee of Taipei's security.}}
# To [[overcome]] an [[abstract]] [[obstacle]].
#: {{ux|en|Today I '''conquered''' my fear of flying by finally boarding a plane.}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''conquer''' difficulties or temptations}}
#* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Regained|1|passage=By winning words to '''conquer''' willing hearts, / And make persuasion do the work of fear.}}
#* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=8|passage=The humor of my proposition appealed more strongly to Miss Trevor than I had looked for, and from that time forward she became her old self again; for, even after she had '''conquered''' her love for the Celebrity, the mortification of having been jilted by him remained.}}
# {{lb|en|dated}} To [[gain]], [[win]], or [[obtain]] by effort.
#: {{ux|en|to '''conquer''' freedom;   to '''conquer''' a peace}}
